name: SE555DR
title: NA555, NE555, SA555, SE555 precision timers
summary: The bipolar 555 timer in four temperature grades. A resistor and capacitor set a one-shot delay, or two resistors and one capacitor set the frequency and duty cycle of a free-running oscillator; trigger and threshold sit near one third and two thirds of VCC and can be moved through CONT. The output sinks or sources up to 200 mA from a 4.5 V to 16 V supply (SE555 18 V). NA555DR is the -40 °C to 105 °C grade in SOIC-8 on a 2500-piece reel.
key_figures: 4.5 V to 16 V (SE555 4.5 V to 18 V)

notes: The four grades differ in operating temperature range: NA555 -40 °C to 105 °C, NE555 0 °C to 70 °C, SA555 -40 °C to 85 °C, SE555 -55 °C to 125 °C. SE555 also has a supply limit of 18 V instead of 16 V and tighter limits on several electrical parameters.
Packages by grade: NA555 in D (SOIC-8) and P (PDIP-8); NE555 in D, P, PS (SO-8) and PW (TSSOP-8); SA555 in D and P; SE555 in D, FK (LCCC-20), JG (CDIP-8) and P.
A logo, lot trace code or environmental mark may appear on a part beside the listed marking.
SE555 also exists as SE555M (military, QML) and SE555-SP (space, radiation tolerant, ceramic) versions.

circuits.title: Circuit for monostable operation
circuits.description: One-shot. A falling edge on the input pulls TRIG below one third of VCC, the output goes high and the discharge switch lets go of C, which charges through RA. When C reaches two thirds of VCC the threshold comparator ends the pulse, the output falls and DISCH empties C. Pulse length is about 1.1 × RA × C. RESET is tied to VCC and CONT goes to ground through a capacitor.

circuits.title: Circuit for astable operation
circuits.description: Free-running oscillator. TRIG and THRES are joined on the timing capacitor, so C swings between one third and two thirds of VCC: it charges through RA and RB while the output is high and discharges through RB alone into DISCH while the output is low. RL pulls the output up to VCC. CONT is left open; a capacitor from CONT to ground is optional. A 0.01 µF capacitor sits from VCC to ground.

circuits.title: Circuit for missing-pulse detector
circuits.description: A retriggerable one-shot that flags a gap in a pulse train. Each low input pulse both triggers the timer and turns on the PNP transistor, which dumps the timing capacitor; while pulses keep arriving faster than the RA·C interval the output stays high. If a pulse is missing, or the gap is too long, C reaches the threshold and the output drops low. RL is an output pull-up and CONT is bypassed with 0.01 µF.

circuits.title: Circuit for pulse-width modulation
circuits.description: A clock train triggers the monostable on TRIG while a signal on CONT moves the threshold, so the width of each output pulse follows the modulation voltage. RA and C set the nominal width; RL is an output pull-up.

circuits.title: Circuit for pulse-position modulation
circuits.description: An astable oscillator whose CONT pin carries a modulation signal. Moving CONT moves both capacitor thresholds, so the timing of each output pulse, and with it frequency and duty cycle, follows the modulation. RA, RB and C set the free-running frequency; RL is an output pull-up.

circuits.title: Sequential timer circuit
circuits.description: Three monostables in a chain. Closing S grounds the first TRIG and starts timer A. When output A falls at the end of its interval, the 0.001 µF capacitor and 33 kΩ pull-up turn the edge into a short low pulse on the next TRIG, which starts timer B; B starts C the same way. Each stage's interval is 1.1 × R × C of its own timing pair, and each CONT is bypassed with 0.01 µF.

operation.text: A bipolar timer for delays from about 10 µs to hours and oscillation from below 1 mHz to 100 kHz. An internal resistor divider sets a threshold level near two thirds of VCC and a trigger level near one third; the two comparators drive a latch that controls the output stage and the discharge transistor. CONT gives access to the two-thirds point so both levels can be shifted. Output and discharge sink capability rise with VCC.

RESET overrides TRIG, and TRIG overrides THRES. With RESET low the latch is reset: output low, discharge on. TRIG below its level sets the output high and releases the discharge; THRES above its level, with TRIG above its own, resets the output low and turns the discharge on.
The output sinks or sources up to 200 mA. At VCC = 5 V its levels suit TTL inputs. Operation is specified from 5 V to 15 V supply.

A timing cycle starts once TRIG falls below the trigger level. To end at the expected time, TRIG must have returned high at least 10 µs before the interval runs out. With TRIG grounded, comparator storage time can reach 10 µs, so the shortest one-shot pulse is about 10 µs. Because both threshold and charging rate scale with VCC, the interval does not depend on supply voltage provided VCC holds steady during it.

Pulling RESET and TRIG low together in the middle of an interval discharges C and restarts timing when RESET rises again; until then the output is held low. An unused RESET is tied straight to VCC to avoid false triggering; a RESET that is driven is pulled up to VCC through an external resistor. Unused inputs in general should sit at a defined logic level.

Adding RB between DISCH and the capacitor and joining TRIG to THRES makes the timer retrigger itself. C charges through RA plus RB and discharges through RB only, between about 0.67 × VCC and 0.33 × VCC, so RA and RB alone fix duty cycle and frequency, whatever the supply voltage. Keep the frequency at or below 100 kHz to limit waveform distortion; above that the TLC555 CMOS timer is the suggested part.

The monostable cannot be retriggered while it is timing, so an interval longer than the input period turns it into a frequency divider. Divide-by-three example: VCC = 5 V, RA = 1250 Ω, C = 0.2 µF in the monostable circuit.
Supply range is 4.5 V to 16 V, or 18 V for SE555. A bypass capacitor from VCC to GND is strongly advised; 0.1 µF ceramic is enough.
Typical curve data below -40 °C or above 105 °C applies only to SE555.
